author: @wassimyounes_
title_or_hook: OpenAI GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch summary
summary: Launch-day summary of OpenAI's two new models released Tue Nov 17: GPT-6.2 Astra (flagship) and GPT-6.2 Sol (cheaper everyday model), rolling out across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API. Verified routing facts: Astra scores 62 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, number 2 overall behind Claude Fable 5.2, passing Gemini 4 Carbon (60) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59). Astra API price is $8/$40 per million input/output tokens, 20 percent below GPT-6 Astra, cached input down to $0.40 from $1.00. Sol is $2/$10, unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol, reaches Intelligence Index 57 (about GPT-6 Astra level) at about 15 percent of Astra-class cost per task. Artificial Analysis weighted cost per Index task: Astra $4.00, Sol $1.01. Corrections: the caption's coding scores do not match AA's Coding Agent Index, where Astra is flat versus GPT-6 Astra and Sol loses 3 points versus GPT-6.1 Sol; the caption's $26.54 Fable per-task figure is UNVERIFIED. Hallucination rates at max effort per AA: Astra 59 percent, Sol 55 percent (AA-Omniscience). System card classifies both models Critical for cybersecurity capability. First test: run 5 real fleet tasks on Sol via the API and compare cost and pass against the current default route.

Weighted cost per Index task: Astra $4.00, Sol $1.01 (Artificial Analysis)

summary: Kennedy Space Center countdown clock post nodding to Voyager 1, which reaches one light-day from Earth early Wednesday morning. Verified at NASA: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day at 5:16:07 a.m. EST on Wed Nov 18, 2026, about 16.1 billion miles (25.9 billion km); a radio signal then needs a full 24 hours each way. NASA invited the public to mark it Tue Nov 17 night by shining a light skyward (Shine Bright for Voyager's Light-Day, flashing V-G-R in Morse), with a JPL discussion Thu Nov 19. The post's comparison is correct: Earth is about 8.3 light-minutes from the Sun. Household and science interest; a genuinely dated, checkable event.
